title: Mismatch repair protein MLH1 controls testis development by regulating the Hippo-YAP signaling pathway.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (2.15 MB) and the inner gkag883_supplemental_files.zip: it holds exactly two files, 'Table S1.pdf' and 'Revised Suppl Figures for NAR-01035-Q-2026.R1.pdf', plus the seven main figure images. I extracted the text of Table S1 and it is a reagents list (antibody names, vendors such as Cell Signaling Technology and Santa Cruz, catalogue numbers, PCR primers) with no measurements. Searched the full open-access text for the words RNA-seq, transcriptome, GEO, GSE, ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN, proteomic and single-cell: zero hits. NCBI link-out from the paper returned only the PubMed Central record, no GEO, SRA, BioProject or dbGaP entry, and a DOI search of Zenodo/Dryad returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology (MLH1 binding YAP via its C-terminal domain, competition with LATS1 phosphorylation, partial rescue of testis hypoplasia by MST1/2 inhibition) is read from the abstract and text only; all of it rests on Western blots, immunostaining and quantitative PCR bar charts shown as images, not as numbers I could open.

a1_downloadable.note: Nothing to download. The data availability statement says 'All data are available in the main text and/or Supplementary Materials', and the supplement I unzipped is two PDFs: a reagents table and a figure pack. No repository accession of any kind exists for this paper (checked NCBI link-out and Zenodo/Dryad by DOI).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table, so there is no column. Any prediction target (for example band intensity for phosphorylated YAP, or germ-cell counts) would have to be hand-digitised from figure images, which is construction, not extraction.

a3_inputs_present.note: No per-example inputs exist in machine-readable form. The only sequences in the paper are genotyping primers in Table S1; protein sequences for MLH1, YAP, LATS1 and TEAD would have to be pulled from UniProt separately.

a4_units_stated.note: Units appear only as axis labels inside figure images (relative expression, fold change), with no units column anywhere because there is no data file.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero machine-readable rows. The experimental unit is a mouse or a culture well; the paper's biggest-sounding experiments involve a handful of animals per genotype, far under the ~400-row floor for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, but only because there is no data; passing this says nothing in favour of the paper.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is physical (immunoblots, immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR), so not circular, but the values exist only as rendered figure pixels, so no label can be traced to a number.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper publishes no machine-readable measurements, so no model could be trained or tested on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and domain content to predict which proteins bind and stabilise YAP, a growth-control switch.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would have needed many protein pairs labelled as binding or not binding YAP, with each protein's amino-acid sequence as input. This paper supplies exactly one such pair (MLH1 with YAP), so the usable example count here is effectively zero.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given protein binds YAP's WW domains and blocks its phosphorylation by the kinase LATS1. The ground truth in this paper comes from co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot images, which are not available as numbers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer and developmental biology labs would like to know which other proteins hijack the Hippo-YAP switch, but that project would have to be built from protein-interaction databases, not from this paper.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. A protein-protein interaction or kinase-substrate predictor touching Hippo-YAP would have to be assembled from external resources (BioGRID, IntAct, PhosphoSitePlus); this paper would at best contribute a single hand-curated positive example.

effort.compute_note: Only the 1.3 MB supplement was opened; no modelling workload was estimated because no dataset exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and list the files - it took one minute and revealed two PDFs and no data table.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic mouse-genetics and biochemistry paper with no deposited data: the whole supplement is a reagents PDF plus figure images, there is no accession in any repository, and every measurement lives inside a blot or a bar chart. Part A fails at A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A7, so scoring stopped there.
